overview: Rwanda is one of Africa's clearest femtech and women's health innovation hubs, anchored by Kasha, the continent's first femtech e-commerce platform and the largest-ever funding round for a woman-founded African healthtech firm. The state has paired this with world-leading public infrastructure: Zipline drone delivery of blood and oxytocin that has sharply cut postpartum-hemorrhage deaths, nationwide digital tools for community health workers, and a first-in-Africa HPV programme now driving toward cervical cancer elimination by 2027. A 2024 landmark law expanded adolescent access to reproductive services without parental consent. Kigali's Norrsken House and HealthTech Hub Africa give the ecosystem a startup engine.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent developments span funding, policy and public-health milestones.

items.text: Rwanda hosts the Africa HealthTech Summit 2025 in Kigali and champions Digital Public Infrastructure for connected, inclusive health systems.
By October 2025, roughly 1.63 million women (30% of those eligible) had been screened for cervical cancer using HPV DNA tests.
Rwanda's Ministry of Health launches Mission 2027, the Accelerated Plan for Elimination of Cervical Cancer, targeting elimination three years ahead of the WHO goal.
Kasha launches Operation SHE (Sustainable Health Equitably) Africa, a private-sector collective to keep HIV, malaria and reproductive-health supplies flowing after the USAID Stop Work Order.
French pharma group Sanofi's Global Health Unit makes a strategic equity investment in Kasha to expand delivery of chronic-disease and women's-health products across Africa.
Rwanda's Parliament passes a landmark health law giving adolescents aged 15+ access to contraception and reproductive services without parental consent.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Government policy underpins the country's women's health gains.

items.text: Accelerated Plan for Elimination of Cervical Cancer 2024-2027 (Mission 2027) commits to surpass WHO 90-70-90 targets, building on a first-in-Africa HPV vaccination programme launched in 2011.
New health law lets adolescents 15+ access contraception, HIV prevention and reproductive services without parental consent, and sets a framework for assisted reproductive technologies.
The CEDAW Committee recommends Rwanda remove parental-consent barriers for 16-17 year-olds, following a shadow report by the Center for Reproductive Rights, HDI and GLIHD.
FP2030 commitment: raise modern contraceptive prevalence among married women toward 64% and integrate rights-based reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health strategy.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Kigali's hubs and platforms are scaling women's and maternal health tools.

items.text: HealthTech Hub Africa, at Norrsken House Kigali, hosts up to 30 sub-Saharan health startups with funding, masterclasses and mentorship; its 2025 cohort was opened for applications.
TIP Global Health's E-Heza Data Solutions, a point-of-care app for frontline health workers, has improved care for over 112,000 mothers and children and was selected for HealthTech Hub Africa.
Rwanda's community health workers moved from paper registers to a digital community electronic medical record, scaling toward 58,567 CHWs across 30 districts by end-2026 with UNICEF support.
Kasha expanded operations beyond Rwanda and Kenya into South Africa, DRC, Burundi, Tanzania, Uganda and West Africa, reaching customers via 200+ trained women agents.
Babyl, a digital telemedicine provider partnered with the government, delivers remote consultations reaching women nationwide.
